body: Tested locally, it mostly works as expected. **Testing project:** [test_shadow_stability_2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29363948/test_shadow_stability_2.zip) There's an issue where at wide aspect ratios (like in the editor with a tall Output panel), large shaded rectangles of the shadow map become visible at the edges. Since the shadow map quality is higher, it's likely that the computed FOV isn't high enough to cover the entire frustum here. If you set Min FOV high enough, it will eventually match the result in `master` with no artifacts and similar shadow quality. For reference, I've set the 3D editor camera FOV set to 85 degrees (the default is 70 degrees). `master` | This PR | This PR with high Min FOV -|-|- | | ## Preview *Watch in fullscreen to notice shifting shadow map pixels more easily.* *Minimum FOV is set to 85 degrees in this example (the highest value reached by the animation). ### Keep Height (Hor+) #### Before https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eae14d3c-6fe5-4431-a800-07acf47342e8 #### After https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4555f25-cd64-4c0c-9127-30174347b72f ### Keep Width (Vert-) #### Before https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a48866f7-ba00-43d1-b6ac-875a4b4b7f1b #### After https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3781dcac-ec33-48ac-8c51-b5cf374ed654

Works great now (also in Frustum mode) 🙂 I've tested aspect ratios as wide as 48:9 and it looked correct.

However, I noticed the property has no effect in Orthogonal mode. Should there be a `directional_shadow_min_size` property that's analog to `directional_shadow_min_fov`? This would be used in Orthogonal mode to compute a minimum shadow FOV, avoiding flicker during zoom transitions.
